newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO resume Hebron talks in Jericho.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO resume Hebron talks in Jericho.

text.p: Israeli-Palestinian negotiations on an overdue Israeli redeployment in the occupied West Bank town of Hebron resumed on Sunday with officials predicting no early agreement.
"It will take a long time," Israeli chief negotiator Dan Shomron told reporters before the talks at the Palestinian Ministry of Local Government in autonomous Jericho.
The last bargaining round on Thursday, attended by U.S. diplomats, failed to bring the sides closer together.
Palestinian officials blamed Israel's insistence that its soldiers be allowed to re-enter the 80 percent of Hebron due to be handed over to PLO police.

"The Israelis will not find any Palestinian who would accept the principle of giving Israelis the right to re-enter Palestinian areas after the handover," PLO Preventive Security Chief in Gaza Mohammad Dahlan told Reuters.
"We will continue to reject this principle and they had better stop asking for it if they want an agreement," he said.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has rejected any renegotiation of the Hebron accord, which was signed last year by a left-centre Israeli government ousted in May by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Netanyahu seeks to alter the Hebron deal to give more protection to some 400 militant Jewish settlers who live and study in heavily guarded enclaves among the more than 100,000 Palestinians of the town.
Under the interim PLO-Israel peace deal, Hebron was to be handed over to Palestinian self-rule last year, but Israel delayed the transfer for security reasons.

PLO chief negotiator Saeb Erekat said Palestinian and Israeli teams were preparing letters of assurances to be exchanged between Arafat and Netanyahu. He said Palestinians wanted guarantees of continued implementation of peace deals made earlier with Israel.

"We submitted a list of issues we want mentioned in the letter, which include specifying dates for resumption of final status talks, dates for talks on implementing interim ourstanding issues which require further negotiations and dates for implementing issues that don't require further negotiation."

Israeli spokesman Moshe Fogel said of Israel's letter wanted from Palestinians: "The principle of reciprocity is a point we believe is an integral part of the agreements, and we want Palestinians to live up to the agreements".

"Prime Minister Netanyahu said many times he was willing to live up to the agreements, but there are a series of Palestinian violations of the agreement and a number of issues that Palestinians have to address," Fogel told Reuters.
